Definition: to flit, i.e. vanish away (subside, escape; causatively, chase, impel, deliver)
BiblicalUsage: Nus is to flee, to run away, to escape, to vanish from before something stronger. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee in Genesis 14:10, and Moses flees from the serpent his own rod has become in Exodus 4:3. Leviticus 26:17 warns of a worse flight, fleeing when no one pursues, and Numbers 10:35 turns the word into a prayer: when the ark sets forward, let those who hate the Lord flee before Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fleeing is never neutral in Scripture: men flee from danger, from guilt, and from God, and God Himself scatters His enemies before Him. My position is that the only safe flight is toward Him, because every other direction ends with nowhere left to run.
